reviews.summary: Answers the search at once and is usable tonight. Asked to say that Stardew Valley needs a copy each (text and table) and that Lichess correspondence games need a free account.

Free games, templates, scheduling, planner and links check out against the code; EA and Jackbox claims stay within their pages. Fixes: the soft truth or dare has in-person dares, so it doesn't simply 'play well on camera'; 'you both answer' doesn't fit truth or dare; Stardew needs a copy each and a Jackbox guest needs only a phone; Draw it blind instructions were confusing; Spanish calques ('en las dos puntas', 'planear alrededor de', 'mandar en cámara') and an ambiguous H2.

Matches the intent and beats the listicles with playable two-phone games and the time table. Asked to answer the 'Is sexting good for LDR?' PAA directly, and to add charades and a turn-based phone game, which top results cover.

reviews.summary: All round-1 fixes in. The page I'd send a friend: the top results are long lists of game names, while this says what each game needs and costs, who has to own it, and which fits the 5, 15 or 60 minutes you have tonight, with free games you start from one link.

All round-1 fixes in and correct; new lines (charades, Words With Friends/Apalabrados, Lichess account, sexting FAQ) check out. Two accuracy fixes in EN+ES: a Jackbox guest also needs a screen for the call, not only a phone; drawing blind needs a pen, so it isn't 'nothing at all' in the takeaway and FAQ.

Round-1 fixes in. Beats the top results as the one page that sorts games by the time you have tonight, with cost and setup for each and real free games playable from one link, and it answers every on-topic People also ask question.

reviews.summary: It sorts long distance games by the time you actually have and gives real compatibility checks and free no-install games, instead of a padded list of 50 ideas with an app pitch.

Every product claim matches the code and the external game facts are accurate and qualified; it beats the top results by saying exactly what each game needs and who has to own it, which generic listicles skip.

It sorts games by the time you have, gives free two-phone games from one link, and covers time zones and turn-based play, which the generic listicles skip; every on-topic People also ask question is answered.
